text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif instructed the Chief Election Commissioner to arrange voting rights for 3.5 million Pakistanis living abroad.
- Benazir Bhutto denied reports she intended to give up leadership of the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) in favour of someone from Punjab province.
- The government will launch an efficient programme to provide healthcare services, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- PPP leader Benazir Bhutto accused President Farooq Leghari of "unconstitutional tapping" of her telephone at her residence in Islamabad.
- The coming months will be crucial for the Nawaz Sharif government because debt servicing may eat up all or most of Pakistan's meagre foreign exchange reserves.
- Analysts from foreign fund houses do not agree with a report by Credit Lyonnais Asian Securities warning their clients that Pakistan might default on debt service payments.
- Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) has allowed two-way conversion between internationally traded Global Depository Receipts and locally traded PTCL shares.
- Pakistan's foreign currency reserves have held firm around $1 billion despite some big loan repayments made in the last week of February and first week of March.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto has been elected as life chairperson of her Pakistan People's Party.
- The state-run Water and Power Development Authority and Karachi Electric Supply Corporation owe more than 10 bnillion rupees to oil and gas supply companies and corporations.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will personally receive donations for his debt retirement scheme every day from 9.30 to 10 a.m.
- The chairman of the prime minister's Inspection Commission Abdul Majeed Malik said the government might disband the Federal Investigation Agency and the Intelligence Bureau.
